findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct AC3's rationale to note terraform-drift.yml's push trigger is `branches: [main]` + `paths: ['infra/terraform/**']` (not branches-only), and confirm that dropping it is intended given the path-filtered pull_request trigger still covers infra changes.
evidence: AC3: "codeql.yml and terraform-drift.yml have no push trigger at all (each had only branches: [main], so there is no other branch to preserve)"
terraform-drift.yml lines 15-17: `push:` / `branches: [main]` / `paths: ['infra/terraform/**']` — the push trigger carries a paths filter, not only a branches filter
codeql.yml lines 11-12 DO match AC3 (push has only `branches: [main]`), so the imprecision is specific to terraform-drift.yml
findings.finding: AC3's justification misstates terraform-drift.yml's current push trigger: it claims 'each had only branches: [main], so there is no other branch to preserve', but terraform-drift.yml's push trigger is branches: [main] plus paths: ['infra/terraform/**']. The prescribed action (drop the push key outright) is still correct — the path-filtered pull_request trigger preserves infra-change coverage — but the recorded rationale is inaccurate about the file it edits.
scenarios: An implementer reading AC3 verbatim to reconstruct the pre-change state of terraform-drift.yml would record a wrong 'resulting on: block' rationale in the change (Verification section requires this per-workflow)
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC3 to: 'codeql.yml (push had only branches:[main]) and terraform-drift.yml (push was branches:[main] + paths:[infra/terraform/**]) both drop their push key entirely; terraform-drift.yml's path-filtered pull_request trigger continues to gate infra changes pre-merge.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `actions: read` to test.yml's permissions (or scope it to the main-health-report job) so AC11's Actions-API run-history read succeeds, matching the repo idiom in reconcile-bridge-canary.yml / gerrit-verify.yaml / codeql.yml; without it AC11/AC12 permanently fall through to the AC14 placeholder.
evidence: AC11: 'The last-known-green main SHA is resolved from the workflow's own successful run history via the Actions API (status=success on the current branch).'

Repo invariant: reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:60 `actions: read   # read reconcile-bridge.yml run history`; gerrit-verify.yaml:38 `actions: read   # workflow-conclusion queries this run's jobs`; codeql.yml:32 `actions: read` — every run-history reader pairs the read with this scope.
AC14 treats a failing API call (incl. 403) as a graceful-degrade path, so the missing scope would be masked as a permanent placeholder rather than surfaced as an error.
findings.finding: AC11's mechanism — the main-health-report job resolving last-known-green via the Actions API from within test.yml — will always fail the API call and permanently degrade to the AC14 placeholder, because test.yml grants only `contents: read` and the plan never adds the `actions: read` permission that every other run-history-reading workflow in this repo declares.
scenarios: A green scheduled run tries to publish its SHA as last-known-green (AC12) but the API read 403s for lack of `actions: read`, so no lower bound is ever established.
A red run emits a bisect recipe with the placeholder lower bound (AC14) on every failure, never the real last-known-green SHA — the AC13 one-copy-paste remediation is defeated.
findings.suggested_fix: In test.yml, either raise the top-level block to `permissions:\n  contents: read\n  actions: read` or give the new main-health-report job its own `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }`. Add an AC asserting the report job runs with `actions: read`.
